name: Provider routing, fallback, retry and cost correctness
purpose: routing, tier fallback, retry, cost and pricing arithmetic on offline cases (fake and dry-run providers) Read in this direction: minimise cost per passing task by using the cheapest tier that passes; maximise availability through retry and tier fallback, and keep vendors swappable by configuration alone. The price table covers input tokens only, and no live latency or pass rate per tier is seen, which needs real calls at each tier.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of each implementation on the same cases, with the recorded cost as the tie-break; each run is one row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash, and the leaderboard compares rows only when the hash matches.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the multi_provider offline arm of model_providers runs the whole case set with no model call]

name: Channel transport conformance to the gateway wire contract
purpose: offline cases with a fake MCP gateway: ordered inbound messages, key-spelling drift, non-message and malformed events, wire failure and dead gateway, long-poll clamp, attachments, send args and ids, allowed tools only, close The payload shapes are tolerant guesses (no live gateway was available), so the result is conformance to those shapes, and there is only one channel.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of the live implementation on the rule's cases, recorded as a row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash; a rule holds or does not, so the implementations are never ranked and a deliberately broken baseline must fail the same cases.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new alternative is described: rate its description on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the openclaw_bridge offline arm of talk_over_a_channel runs the whole case set with no model call] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=a single real case runs end to end and is hand-read: esoi run talk_over_a_channel --impl real_gateway --only CHN-001 --max-calls 0]

name: Overseer digest evidence and signal correctness on labelled scenarios
purpose: digest evidence on hand-labelled scenarios (contrast pairs), offline; signal match in a live arm; signal parsing and degrade-to-proceed in judges The signal match itself needs a model and is not seen offline. The digest sheds history operations first and prior escalations last, so the refusal rule keeps its evidence.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of each implementation on the same cases, with the recorded cost as the tie-break; each run is one row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash, and the leaderboard compares rows only when the hash matches.
disadvantages: It cannot see whether a signal improved a run: the offline arm checks only that the digest holds the evidence a label turns on, the live signal arm has never been recorded, and no run with the overseer is compared with the same run without it, so the overseer's value net of its cost is unknown while it runs by default. The measure the owner's definition needs (per risk category, the selected response against no response with a significance test, and its effect on the overall QAR metric) is not built.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new alternative is described: rate its description on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the digest_probe offline arm of overseer_signals runs the whole case set with no model call] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=a single real case runs end to end and is hand-read: esoi run overseer_signals --impl live_model --only OVS-001 --max-calls 2] > live [real=yes | max-age-days=90 | when=a person approved the spend under the metric run policy]
command: esoi run overseer_signals --impl live_model; esoi run overseer_signals --impl digest_probe

name: Cost, budget and resource-guard correctness
purpose: offline cases: price per provider and model (including unknown model and provider), bootstrap cost estimate, provider detection from the environment, daily budget (limit, off, bad value, negative tokens, restart reload), and resource-guard hysteresis for memory, free memory and load; zero model calls Read in this direction: maximise correctness of per-model price lookup with a stated default for unknown models; maximise budget accuracy across restarts and day boundaries; minimise flapping of the host guard by using hysteresis. Prices are a hand-kept snapshot of list prices (input tokens only), so a provider price change is not noticed until the table is edited.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of the live implementation on the rule's cases, recorded as a row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash; a rule holds or does not, so the implementations are never ranked and a deliberately broken baseline must fail the same cases.

name: Supported and calibrated answers to world questions
purpose: Measures whether claims about the world are supported by a cited source and stated with a confidence that matches the evidence. Read in this direction: maximise supported claims; minimise the gap between stated confidence and how often claims hold; minimise cost per answer.
record: Per implementation on the same labelled world questions: the share of claims supported by a cited source, a calibration error over stated confidence, and cost per answer; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet. Reference evidence strength is set by the case author; a supported claim can still be the wrong advice for the person; a live research source makes runs differ over time.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the web_with_support_check offline arm of know_the_world runs the whole case set with no model call]

name: Hub of hubs
purpose: Measures, offline, how far QAR is a hub of hubs. Per area of the hub registry eight checks hold or not: a hub is registered or none is recorded as existing, at least half the wired hub connections (a connection is a class gained through one hub, never one service) need no code, no single-service integration is hand-wired where a hub covers it unless waived with a reason, research is within 90 days, the area has one seam in code, its hub is selectable by metric, core holds no vendor branch for it, and a fake hub added through its configuration entry works with zero library edits. Read in this direction: coverage, integration by configuration and freshness up, vendor branches down.
record: Per area and check pass or fail with the reason; coverage; the share of capabilities needing no code per integration; days since research per area (oldest and mean); the vendor branches found in core with file and line; the combined score; one row per run pinned to the commit and cases hash, no model call. The floor is run by hand (esoi run hub_of_hubs --impl hub_of_hubs.broken.vendor_grep:build).
disadvantages: Freshness is the date a person or the autopilot recorded, not proof that the research was good; findings are from secondary web results; a probe exists for four of ten areas; the capability list is hand-kept.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the registry_scan offline arm of hub_of_hubs runs the whole case set with no model call]

name: Intents whose solutions one paragraph and one diagram explain as the code builds them
purpose: Every intent's solutions are explained by one coherent paragraph and one diagram that match how they relate in the records and in the code, in a hierarchy a reader can take in.
record: Per intent, from `python3 -m esoi.coherence --json`: whether solution_coherence names every solution and states every uses edge in one sentence, the roots and the solutions no edge reaches, whether solution_diagram draws exactly the uses edges with what each passes, the share of uses edges with both ends in code that the code shows, the share of import edges between the intent's solutions that a uses path covers, the largest fan-out and the depth.
disadvantages: Reads the selected implementation's uses only; the code evidence is an import, a named id or interface, or an Assembler over declared seats, not a proof that one part calls the other; QAR composes many parts through its configuration modules, which this stage counts only where the user's own module names the part.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=python3 -m esoi.coherence --gate exits 0 on the committed records (the floors of [rules.S39] in esoi.toml, measured when the tree was recorded, raised as the composition is typed, never lowered) after any change to a solution, an implementation's uses or the intent's paragraph or diagram]
